LAB EXPERIMENT No. 1
I. Introduction to Matrix Laboratory (MATLAB)

MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a high-level numerical computing environment widely used in engineering, science, and applied mathematics. It is designed primarily for matrix-based computations, making it ideal for solving numerical methods problems efficiently and accurately. MATLAB provides built-in functions for matrix manipulation, data visualization, numerical analysis, and algorithm development. Its interactive environment allows users to rapidly prototype solutions and analyze numerical results with minimal programming overhead.

Typical uses of MATLAB include solving systems of equations, numerical integration, optimization, signal processing, and modeling physical systems. In numerical methods, MATLAB serves as an essential computational tool for implementing algorithms and validating analytical solutions.
Objectives
At the end of this experiment, the students should be able to:
Become familiar with the MATLAB environment, interface, and command window.
Understand MATLAB syntax and basic commands.
Perform simple numerical and matrix-based computations.
Use MATLAB as a tool for solving numerical methods problems.
MATLAB Windows

MATLAB provides an integrated working environment known as the MATLAB Desktop, which consists of several interactive windows. These windows help users efficiently write commands, manage files, and analyze data. The major components of the MATLAB Desktop are described below.
1. MATLAB Desktop
The MATLAB Desktop is the main interface that appears automatically when MATLAB is launched. It contains several sub-windows that support numerical computation and program development.
a) Command Window
The Command Window is the primary working area in MATLAB where users enter commands and execute functions. It is identified by the MATLAB command prompt (>>).

The output of executed commands is displayed in this window, except for graphical outputs, which appear in a separate Figure Window. Commands entered in the Command Window cannot be edited once executed.
b) Current Directory

The Current Directory window displays the list of files and folders available in the active working directory. It is typically located on the left side of the MATLAB Desktop.Using this window, users can manage files such as M-files by right-clicking to run, rename, delete, or perform other file-related operations.
c) Workspace

The Workspace window shows all variables currently stored in memory during a MATLAB session. It displays essential information such as the variable name, data type, and size. This window helps users monitor and manage the variables generated while executing MATLAB commands.
d) Command History

The Command History window keeps a record of all commands entered during the MATLAB session. Users can reuse previous commands by selecting them from this list.Additionally, commands from the Command History can be copied and saved as an M-file, allowing users to create scripts and maintain a record of executed MATLAB functions.
